thread:
Alex: Heads-up — ran into a numeric blowup on a long-context job with llmx-13B-q4f16 (dedicated pool). Model output went to gibberish, and we saw infs from softmax in the fused flash kernel.
Tanya: Can you paste the raw logs + config? seq_len, batching, kernel selector flags?
Alex: Quick summary: single convo ~12k tokens, kv-paged enabled, fp8 fallback toggled off, batch_size=1, prefer_flash=true. Logs snippet below (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] max_logit=812.345, min_logit=-23.2
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] softmax out: inf, nans detected
[2026-02-28T14:12:03Z] kernel: fused_flash_softmax.cu: line 342: exp overflow
```
Jia: That max_logit is massive — typical exp() overflow territory. If scale on QK multiplies due to quantization scaling we can hit this easily on long sequences (cache concat causes growth).
Sam: Reproduced locally with a minimal script. Repro code:
```
# repro.py (minimal)
model = load_model("llmx-13b-q4f16")
ctx = LargeChatContext(max_tokens=13000, kv_paged=True)
input = "hello" * 5000
out = model.generate(input, batch_size=1)
# observe softmax infs in logs
```
perf-bot: CI run results (2026-02-28T15:00Z): baseline p95=48ms, after forcing stable softmax kernel p95=54ms (+12.5%). Full trace: https://ci/reports/rt/21876
Tanya: Mitigation options we discussed before: 1) pre-softmax clamp (e.g., clamp logits to [-30, +30]) 2) fall back to numerically-stable softmax (log-sum-exp) kernel when logits range exceeds threshold 3) rescale QK when merging KV cache pages. Tradeoffs: clamp = cheap but can shift distribution; stable kernel = heavier but correct; rescale = subtle but preserves shape if careful.
Alex: I tried clamp [-30,30] on the fused kernel path — removes infs and recovers intelligible output. Throughput hit ~1.2% on our bench long-run (mostly memory-bound), latency p95 increase ~+3ms.
Sam: I prototyped a selector rule: if (max_logit - min_logit) > 40 || seq_len > 4096 => use stable-softmax kernel. Bench: p50 +1.5ms, p95 +5.8ms, but no numeric errors.
Jia: Important note: when we do KV page concatenation we currently do NOT renormalize the merged K/V scale for quantized models. That can amplify magnitude of QK dot product because per-page scale was different. We should apply per-page rescale op at merge-time for q4/q8 families.
Alex: I'll open a small fix: runtime.config.attn_numeric_safety = {enabled: true, logits_range_threshold: 40, force_stable_seq_len: 4096, clamp: [-30,30]} (flags only; defaults off). Add a toggle to kernel selector to prefer stable kernel when flag is on.
Tanya: Please also add an automated unit that synthesizes logits with extreme dynamic range and asserts no inf/nan and that outputs are within eps of stable reference (float64 reference).
Sam: Also add a metric: attn_numeric_safety_triggers_total and a p99 latency bucket for when we fall back, so POs can see customer impact.
Alex: Action items: 1) @Alex open PR with: (a) clamp path + selector rule, (b) unit test with synthetic extreme logits, (c) prom metric. 2) @Jia prototype KV-page rescale at merge and add quant test vectors. 3) @Sam run extended perf sweep across models and commit types.
Jia: One more micro-observation — fp16/bf16 vs q4 show different behavior: bf16 tends to surface smaller peaks but the fused kernel had an unchecked exp() call regardless of dtype. Need guard in kernel itself (cheap clamp before exp).
Tanya: Good. If kernel-level guard is cheap we should land that ASAP; higher-level selector is a fallback for perf reasons. Document tradeoffs in the changelog and perf notes.
Alex: I'll include a short doc blurb in the PR describing when this triggers (long-convos, heterogeneous kv-page scales, aggressive quantization) and recommended runtime knobs for customers.
Sam: Sounds good. Please tag the perf numbers in the PR. I'll follow up with a canary on dedicated pools once merged.
Alex: Thanks — opening PR now. cc: @Tanya @Jia @Sam
